addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

## claude.ai Zapier
This server connects you to 9,000+ apps via Zapier.

IMPORTANT: Before calling any tool, ensure you have loaded the available tools from this server (tools/list).

If the user seems new or has no tools enabled, retrieve the "zapier:onboarding" skill using get_zapier_skill and follow its instructions.
Use list_zapier_skills to discover other saved workflows.

## Managing what's enabled

- `inspect_zapier_actions({ selected_api?, action?, tool_name?, params? })` — inspect enabled actions and resolve action parameter schemas. **Returns everything you need to build an execute call**: each action's `app` (display name), `selected_api`, `action` key, `action_type` (exact SDK type), `tool_name`, `params`, inline dynamic enum values when resolvable, and `dynamic_properties_schema` when parent values in `params` are sufficient.
- `discover_zapier_actions({ app? })` — search the Zapier app catalog for actions to enable (`app` is a free-text search query).
- `enable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — add an action (you'll receive a `tools/list_changed` notification afterwards). Pass the `selected_api` returned by `discover_zapier_actions`.
- `disable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — remove an action. Pass the `selected_api` from `inspect_zapier_actions`.

## Executing an action

Always call `inspect_zapier_actions` first to retrieve the action's exact `selected_api`, `action` key, `tool_name`, parameter schema, and any dynamic-argument guidance. Then:

1. If a parameter has `dynamic_enum_values`, use one of those `value` fields. If it has `dynamic_enum_missing_dependencies` or no usable value yet, set the dependency params you know and call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` again. Use `enum_property`, `enum_search`, and `enum_cursor` with the same tool when you need to search or page one dynamic enum.
2. If the action includes `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, settle those parameters' values, then call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` agai… [truncated]

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. # Fleet Wiring — Handoff / Resume Notes

Turning `lab-fleet` from published reference config into **GitOps that Rancher
Fleet deploys** to this cluster. Full plan (private): Cowork workspace
`_portfolio/ash4d-lab/fleet-wiring-plan.md`. This file is the short resume note
for picking the work back up.

## Topology

- **Rancher controller** — `v2.14.2` at `https://rancher.ash4d.com`
  (**192.168.7.148**, separate host). GitRepo/Bundle objects live here.
- **This cluster** — `sdf1`, downstream `c-nnzn9` at **192.168.7.149**.
  `fleet-agent v0.15.2` is Ready but idle — no GitRepo targets it yet.
- Deploy source is **`lab-fleet` directly**, not `ash4d.com/lab` (Fleet doesn't
  init git submodules, so a GitRepo on `ash4d.com` would clone an empty gitlink).
  Public repo → no clone secret needed.

## ✅ Phase 1 — DONE (committed to `main`, not yet pushed)

Every deployable numbered dir has a `fleet.yaml`:

- **Helm bundles** (`takeOwnership: true`, versions pinned to the running
  releases so Fleet adopts instead of upgrading):
  metallb `0.16.1`, longhorn `1.12.0`, nvdp `0.19.2`, dcgm-exporter `4.8.2`,
  ollama `1.67.0` (confirmed live), open-webui `14.8.0`, milvus `5.0.22`.
- **Raw-manifest bundles:** comfyui, indexer, mcp, hermes, emby, node-red,
  resilio, plus metallb pools, the nvidia RuntimeClass, and attu.
- Where a dir had a chart **and** raw manifests, the raw manifests were moved
  into a sibling subdir so each chart owns its own bundle path (Fleet = one
  chart per path): `01-networking/pools/`, `03-gpu/{dcgm-exporter,runtimeclass}/`,
  `06-milvus/attu/`.
- `09-mcp/github-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml` → `.yaml.txt` so Fleet never
  applies the placeholder Secret.
- `00-host` and `14-cluster-mgmt` stay docs-only (no `fleet.yaml`). Traefik is
  k3s-bundled and not Fleet-managed (`traefik-values.yaml` is reference only).

**Not yet pushed** — push `lab-fleet` `main` to the remote before Fleet can
clone it.

## ⏭ Phase 0 — Enable CD on the controller (needs Rancher API token for .148)

1. Mint a Rancher API token (UI: avatar → Account & API Keys → Create API Key,
   no scope), export as `RTOKEN`.
2. Check the `fleet` feature (agent env hinted `fleet=false`); enable if off:
   `PUT https://rancher.ash4d.com/v3/features/fleet -d '{"value":true}'`.
3. Confirm the cluster's Fleet workspace (likely `fleet-default`) and a stable
   target label (e.g. `management.cattle.io/cluster-name: c-nnzn9`).
- **Acceptance:** `GET /v1/fleet.cattle.io.gitrepos` returns 200 and the cluster
  is listed under a Fleet workspace with a targetable label.

## ⏭ Phase 2/3 — GitRepo + staged rollout (needs token; approve each widen)

Create a GitRepo in the Fleet workspace pointing at
`https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet`, branch `main`. **Start narrow** with a
single low-risk `paths:` entry, then widen one component at a time, riskiest
last:

| Order | Component(s) | Risk | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `12-node-red`, `13-resilio`, `11-emby` | low | app layer, easy rollback |
| 2 | `07-comfyui`, `09-mcp`, `10-hermes` | low–med | Secrets must pre-exist |
| 3 | `05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`, `04-ollama` | med | helm adopt; watch pod churn |
| 4 | `01-networking`, `03-gpu` | med–high | MetalLB/Traefik + GPU; net blips |
| 5 | `02-longhorn` | **high** | storage — adopt last, or monitor-only |

At each step: add the path, let Fleet render, confirm the BundleDeployment goes
Ready, spot-check the workload, proceed. Roll back by removing the path.

## Watch-outs

- **Helm adoption is the real hazard.** `helm get manifest` vs `helm template`
  should match before enabling a helm path; adopt one release at a time.
- **Missing Secrets = stuck bundles.** Raw manifests use `secretKeyRef`
  (github-mcp token, open-webui `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY`, hermes Slack/API). Create
  them out-of-band before adding those paths.
- Verify: controller `…/gitrepos/fleet-default/lab-fleet | jq .status.summary`;
  downstream `kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system get bundledeployments -A`.

1	# Startup hook run by comfyui-nvidia-docker's init on every container start
2	# (after venv/ComfyUI setup, before the server launches). Keeps pip deps
3	# self-healing across image upgrades and venv rebuilds.
4	apiVersion: v1
5	kind: ConfigMap
6	metadata:
7	  labels:
8	    app: comfyui
9	  name: comfyui-user-script
10	  namespace: ai
11	data:
12	  user_script.bash: |
13	    #!/bin/bash
14	    set -e
15	    PIP=/comfy/mnt/venv/bin/pip
16	
17	    # 1. Self-heal: ensure every custom node's python deps are present
18	    #    (no-op when satisfied; rebuilds them after a fresh venv).
19	    for req in /basedir/custom_nodes/*/requirements.txt; do
20	      [ -f "$req" ] && $PIP install --no-cache-dir -r "$req"
21	    done
22	
23	    # 2. Version pins LAST so they win over whatever the steps above pulled.
24	    #    torch 2.6 (cu124) breaks with transformers >= 4.54
25	    #    (torch.float8_e8m0fnu). Revisit when the image moves to torch >= 2.7.
26	    $PIP install --no-cache-dir "transformers==4.51.3"
27	---
28	apiVersion: apps/v1
29	kind: Deployment
30	metadata:
31	  labels:
32	    app: comfyui
33	  name: comfyui
34	  namespace: ai
35	spec:
36	  replicas: 1
37	  selector:
38	    matchLabels:
39	      app: comfyui
40	  strategy:
41	    type: Recreate
42	  template:
43	    metadata:
44	      labels:
45	        app: comfyui
46	    spec:
47	      containers:
48	      # NOTE: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (GPU pin) is deliberately NOT managed
49	      # here — it is set live on the cluster and switched between GPUs as
50	      # needed. If a future sync strips it, re-add via kubectl edit/patch.
51	      - env:
52	        - name: COMFY_CMDLINE_EXTRA
53	          value: --listen 0.0.0.0
54	        - name: WANTED_UID
55	          value: '1024'
56	        - name: WANTED_GID
57	          value: '1024'
58	        - name: BASE_DIRECTORY
59	          value: /basedir
60	        - name: SECURITY_LEVEL
61	          value: normal
62	        - name: USE_UV
63	          value: 'true'
64	        image: mmartial/comfyui-nvidia-docker:ubuntu22_cuda12.4.1-latest
65	        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
66	        name: comfyui
67	        ports:
68	        - containerPort: 8188
69	          name: 8188tcp
70	        resources:
71	          limits:
72	            nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
73	          requests:
74	            nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
75	        volumeMounts:
76	        # basedir = models/custom_nodes/outputs; run = venv + ComfyUI + HF
77	        # cache. BOTH must be PVC-backed or installs die with the pod.
78	        - mountPath: /basedir
79	          name: data
80	          subPath: basedir
81	        - mountPath: /comfy/mnt
82	          name: data
83	          subPath: run
84	        - mountPath: /comfy/mnt/user_script.bash
85	          name: user-script
86	          subPath: user_script.bash
87	      runtimeClassName: nvidia
88	      securityContext:
89	        fsGroup: 1024
90	        runAsGroup: 1024
91	        runAsUser: 1024
92	        supplementalGroups:
93	        - 44
94	        - 109
95	      volumes:
96	      - name: data
97	        persistentVolumeClaim:
98	          claimName: comfyui-data
99	      - name: user-script
100	        configMap:
101	          defaultMode: 0o755
102	          name: comfyui-user-script
103	---
104	apiVersion: apps/v1
105	kind: Deployment
106	metadata:
107	  labels:
108	    app: comfyui-filebrowser
109	  name: comfyui-filebrowser
110	  namespace: ai
111	spec:
112	  replicas: 1
113	  selector:
114	    matchLabels:
115	      app: comfyui-filebrowser
116	  template:
117	    metadata:
118	      labels:
119	        app: comfyui-filebrowser
120	    spec:
121	      containers:
122	      - args:
123	        - --root=/srv
124	        - --address=0.0.0.0
125	        - --port=8080
126	        - --database=/config/filebrowser.db
127	        image: filebrowser/filebrowser:latest
128	        name: filebrowser
129	        ports:
130	        - containerPort: 8080
131	        resources:
132	          limits:
133	            cpu: 250m
134	            memory: 256Mi
135	          requests:
136	            cpu: 50m
137	            memory: 64Mi
138	        volumeMounts:
139	        - mountPath: /srv
140	          name: comfyui-data
141	          subPath: basedir
142	        - mountPath: /config
143	          name: fb-config
144	      securityContext:
145	        fsGroup: 1024
146	        runAsGroup: 1024
147	        runAsUser: 1024
148	      volumes:
149	      - name: comfyui-data
150	        persistentVolumeClaim:
151	          claimName: comfyui-data
152	      - emptyDir: {}
153	        name: fb-config
154	---
155	apiVersion: v1
156	kind: Service
157	metadata:
158	  labels:
159	    app: comfyui
160	  name: comfyui
161	  namespace: ai
162	spec:
163	  ports:

# Startup hook run by comfyui-nvidia-docker's init on every container start
# (after venv/ComfyUI setup, before the server launches). Keeps pip deps
# self-healing across image upgrades and venv rebuilds.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui
  name: comfyui-user-script
  namespace: ai
data:
  user_script.bash: |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e
    PIP=/comfy/mnt/venv/bin/pip

    # 1. Self-heal: ensure every custom node's python deps are present
    #    (no-op when satisfied; rebuilds them after a fresh venv).
    for req in /basedir/custom_nodes/*/requirements.txt; do
      [ -f "$req" ] && $PIP install --no-cache-dir -r "$req"
    done

    # 2. Version pins LAST so they win over whatever the steps above pulled.
    #    torch 2.6 (cu124) breaks with transformers >= 4.54
    #    (torch.float8_e8m0fnu). Revisit when the image moves to torch >= 2.7.
    $PIP install --no-cache-dir "transformers==4.51.3"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui
  name: comfyui
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: comfyui
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: comfyui
    spec:
      containers:
      # NOTE: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (GPU pin) is deliberately NOT managed
      # here — it is set live on the cluster and switched between GPUs as
      # needed. If a future sync strips it, re-add via kubectl edit/patch.
      - env:
        - name: COMFY_CMDLINE_EXTRA
          value: --listen 0.0.0.0
        - name: WANTED_UID
          value: '1024'
        - name: WANTED_GID
          value: '1024'
        - name: BASE_DIRECTORY
          value: /basedir
        - name: SECURITY_LEVEL
          value: normal
        - name: USE_UV
          value: 'true'
        image: mmartial/comfyui-nvidia-docker:ubuntu22_cuda12.4.1-latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: comfyui
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8188
          name: 8188tcp
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
          requests:
            nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
        volumeMounts:
        # basedir = models/custom_nodes/outputs; run = venv + ComfyUI + HF
        # cache. BOTH must be PVC-backed or installs die with the pod.
        - mountPath: /basedir
          name: data
          subPath: basedir
        - mountPath: /comfy/mnt
          name: data
          subPath: run
        - mountPath: /comfy/mnt/user_script.bash
          name: user-script
          subPath: user_script.bash
      runtimeClassName: nvidia
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1024
        runAsGroup: 1024
        runAsUser: 1024
        supplementalGroups:
        - 44
        - 109
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: comfyui-data
      - name: user-script
        configMap:
          defaultMode: 0o755
          name: comfyui-user-script
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui-filebrowser
  name: comfyui-filebrowser
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: comfyui-filebrowser
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: comfyui-filebrowser
    spec:
      containers:
      - args:
        - --root=/srv
        - --address=0.0.0.0
        - --port=8080
        - --database=/config/filebrowser.db
        image: filebrowser/filebrowser:latest
        name: filebrowser
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 64Mi
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /srv
          name: comfyui-data
          subPath: basedir
        - mountPath: /config
          name: fb-config
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1024
        runAsGroup: 1024
        runAsUser: 1024
      volumes:
      - name: comfyui-data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: comfyui-data
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: fb-config
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui
  name: comfyui
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8188
  selector:
    app: comfyui
  type: LoadBalancer
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui-filebrowser
  name: comfyui-filebrowser
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: comfyui-filebrowser
  type: LoadBalancer
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: comfyui-data
  namespace: ai
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 150Gi
  storageClassName: longhorn
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: glm-model-pvc
  namespace: ai
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 50Gi

=========== 04-ollama/values.yaml ===========
extraEnv:
# Pins ollama to the Tesla V100 32 GB. Do NOT rely on the device plugin to
# choose: GPU 0 on this node is a GTX 1070 (8 GB), which cannot hold a 30B-class
# model at any useful context. See ollama.gpu.enabled below — the two settings
# are a pair.
- name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
  value: GPU-a69c6398-0353-3234-9f35-af0e02865f33
- name: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES
  value: compute,utility
# -1 = never unload. The first model loaded holds its VRAM indefinitely.
# See the sizing note below for what that costs on a shared box.
- name: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE
  value: "-1"
# ollama sizes the KV cache as num_ctx x num_parallel — each slot reserves the
# full OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH, they do not share one window. Confirmed against
# the live pod 2026-07-30: 262144 ctx x 1 slot held ~30.4 GiB of the V100, so
# 2 slots at that context would need ~43 GiB. 2 x 98304 costs 9.56 GiB of KV.
- name: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL
  value: "2"
# Global DEFAULT context for requests that don't pass num_ctx; ollama clamps
# per model to that model's trained maximum.
#
# 98304 (96k) chosen 2026-07-30. This is per parallel slot, so the real cost is
# 98304 x OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL. Sized for qwen3-coder:30b (see the KV budget
# note below). Still clears the 64k floor that hermes-agent (10-hermes) needs.
#
# Keep this declared in the chart. The live Deployment has drifted twice from
# out-of-band `kubectl edit` (65536 on 2026-07-18, 262144 on 2026-07-29), which
# helm never knew about — an undeclared value gets silently reset to ollama's
# built-in default on the next upgrade.
- name: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH
  value: "98304"
# Both are load-bearing for the context sizing above, NOT optional tuning.
# llama.cpp only honours a quantized KV cache when flash attention is on —
# without FA the cache silently falls back to f16 and doubles.
#
# KV budget for qwen3-coder:30b (Q4_K_M, 48 layers, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128
# -> 49152 KV elements/token). q8_0 is 1.0625 bytes/element = 51 KiB/token:
#      96k x 2 slots ->  9.56 GiB KV   <- current setting
#     112k x 2 slots -> 11.16 GiB KV
#     128k x 2 slots -> 12.75 GiB KV   (no headroom)
#     256k x 1 slot  -> 12.75 GiB KV   (was live; caused CPU offload)
# Weights are 17.3 GiB, leaving roughly 12.9 GiB for KV plus compute buffers
# on the 31.75 GiB V100.
#
# Evidence for moving off 256k — /api/ps on 2026-07-30 at 262144 x 1:
#   size 33354990164 vs size_vram 32617026026 = ~703 MiB resident on CPU,
#   with prompt processing at 152 tok/s and falling as context grew.
- name: OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION
  value: "1"
- name: OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE
  value: q8_0
ollama:
  gpu:
    # false ON PURPOSE, and this is what the cluster actually runs. Setting it
    # true makes the chart request nvidia.com/gpu, at which point the device
    # plugin injects its own NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and may hand out GPU 0
    # (the 8 GB GTX 1070). GPU access here comes from runtimeClassName: nvidia
    # plus the explicit UUID above.
    enabled: false
    number: 1
    type: nvidia
  models:
    pull:
    - llama3.1
    - nomic-embed-text
persistentVolume:
  enabled: true
  # 200Gi is the deployed size. PVCs cannot shrink — this file previously said
  # 100Gi, which would have failed or been silently ignored on upgrade.
  size: 200Gi
  storageClass: longhorn
runtimeClassName: nvidia
service:
  loadBalancerIP: 192.168.7.153
  port: 11434
  type: LoadBalancer
tolerations:
- effect: NoSchedule
  key: nvidia.com/gpu
  operator: Exists

- name: VECTOR_DB
  value: milvus

===== ./01-networking/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — MetalLB (Helm). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# Adopts the hand-installed release; pinned to the running chart so Fleet does
# not upgrade on adoption. IPAddressPool/L2Advertisement are a separate bundle
# under pools/ (they need the MetalLB CRDs to exist first).
# traefik-values.yaml is NOT bundled — Traefik is k3s-bundled and managed via
# k3s HelmChartConfig, not Fleet; the file is kept here for reference only.
defaultNamespace: metallb-system
helm:
  releaseName: metallb
  repo: https://metallb.github.io/metallb
  chart: metallb
  version: "0.16.1"
  valuesFiles:
    - metallb-values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
===== ./01-networking/pools/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — MetalLB IPAddressPool + L2Advertisement (raw manifests).
# Depends on the MetalLB CRDs from the metallb bundle; Fleet retries until they
# exist, so this converges after metallb. Add an explicit dependsOn once the
# parent bundle's generated name is known.
defaultNamespace: metallb-system
===== ./02-longhorn/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Longhorn (Helm). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# HIGHEST-RISK adoption (storage). Roll out last, or keep monitor-only; pinned
# to the running chart so adoption does not trigger an upgrade. values.yaml is
# intentionally empty (chart defaults) but referenced for provenance.
defaultNamespace: longhorn-system
helm:
  releaseName: longhorn
  repo: https://charts.longhorn.io
  chart: longhorn
  version: "1.12.0"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
===== ./03-gpu/dcgm-exporter/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — DCGM exporter (Helm). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# Deployed into cattle-monitoring-system alongside rancher-monitoring.
defaultNamespace: cattle-monitoring-system
helm:
  releaseName: dcgm-exporter
  repo: https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/helm-charts
  chart: dcgm-exporter
  version: "4.8.2"
  valuesFiles:
    - dcgm-exporter-values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
===== ./03-gpu/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — NVIDIA device plugin (Helm). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# dcgm-exporter (Helm) and the cluster-scoped RuntimeClass objects are separate
# bundles under dcgm-exporter/ and runtimeclass/. The RuntimeClass should land
# before nvdp so GPU pods can schedule.
defaultNamespace: nvidia-device-plugin
helm:
  releaseName: nvdp
  repo: https://nvidia.github.io/k8s-device-plugin
  chart: nvidia-device-plugin
  version: "0.19.2"
  valuesFiles:
    - nvdp-values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
===== ./03-gpu/runtimeclass/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — cluster-scoped RuntimeClass objects (nvidia, nvidia-experimental).
# Raw manifest. Must land before nvdp and any GPU workload that sets
# runtimeClassName: nvidia. Cluster-scoped, so defaultNamespace is nominal.
defaultNamespace: kube-system
===== ./04-ollama/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Ollama (Helm). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# Version pinned to 1.67.0, confirmed against the running release (bumped
# 2026-07-18) so Fleet adopts rather than upgrades. V100 pin and OLLAMA_*
# tuning live in values.yaml.
defaultNamespace: ai
helm:
  releaseName: ollama
  repo: https://helm.otwld.com/
  chart: ollama
  version: "1.67.0"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
===== ./05-open-webui/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Open WebUI (Helm). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# StatefulSet-backed chat UI. WEBUI_SECRET_KEY must exist as a k8s Secret before
# this path is enabled, or stored tool credentials break on restart.
defaultNamespace: ai
helm:
  releaseName: open-webui
  repo: https://helm.openwebui.com/
  chart: open-webui
  version: "14.8.0"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
===== ./06-milvus/attu/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Attu, the Milvus admin UI (raw manifest).
# Depends on the milvus bundle (points at MILVUS_URL in the ai namespace).
defaultNamespace: ai
===== ./06-milvus/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Milvus (Helm, standalone). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# Multi-component chart (data/etcd/minio on Longhorn PVCs). Attu (the admin UI)
# is a separate raw-manifest bundle under attu/.
defaultNamespace: ai
helm:
  releaseName: milvus
  repo: https://zilliztech.github.io/milvus-helm/
  chart: milvus
  version: "5.0.22"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
===== ./07-comfyui/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — ComfyUI (raw manifests). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# GTX 1070 via the device plugin; manifests carry their own namespace.
defaultNamespace: ai
===== ./08-indexer/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — k8s-docs-indexer (raw manifest). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# Locally-built image; the Dockerfile/source in this dir are build inputs, not
# deployed by Fleet. Only k8s-docs-indexer.yaml is applied.
defaultNamespace: ai
===== ./09-mcp/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — MCP layer (raw manifests): mcpo, k8s-mcp-server,

# The github-mcp token Secret is referenced by name and must be created
# out-of-band — the example is github-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt,
# renamed to .txt so Fleet never applies it.
defaultNamespace: ai
===== ./10-hermes/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Hermes agent (raw manifest). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# Slack AI agent; Slack/API tokens are referenced as Secrets and must exist
# before this path is enabled or the workload reports not-ready.
defaultNamespace: hermes
===== ./11-emby/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Emby (raw manifest). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# s6-overlay image: starts as root, drops via UID/GID env — no pod-level
# securityContext (that breaks s6). GTX 1070 transcode pinned by UUID.
defaultNamespace: emby
===== ./12-node-red/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Node-RED (raw manifest). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# Lowest-risk adoption; the plan's Phase-3 starting path. Recreate strategy
# (single RWO Longhorn writer).
defaultNamespace: node-red
===== ./13-resilio/fleet.yaml =====
# Fleet bundle — Resilio Sync (raw manifest). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# hostPath-backed (restored identity + sync.conf); Recreate strategy, single
# hostPath writer.
defaultNamespace: resilio

input.content:
# SUSE / openSUSE docs -> Milvus, weekly. Companion to k8s-docs-indexer:
# reuses the same locally-built image, but runs a different entrypoint script
# mounted from a ConfigMap (see the bottom of this file) rather than the one
# baked into the image. DocBook XML + AsciiDoc sources, so the work volume is
# larger (8Gi) and the deadline longer (4h) than the k8s corpus.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob

# Prometheus exporter + pass-through proxy in front of ollama.
#
# Two ports, two jobs:
#   9400  /metrics — polls ollama every 15s for loaded-model / VRAM state
#   9401  proxy    — a transparent reverse proxy to ollama:11434. Clients that
#                    point here instead of at ollama directly get their request
#                    volume and latency counted. The docs-rag MCP server
#                    (09-mcp/docs-rag/) and all three indexers (08-indexer/)
#                    are wired through 9401 for exactly this reason.
#
# Separate bundle path from ../ because 04-ollama is a Helm bundle and Fleet
# allows one chart per path. Same split as 06-milvus/attu and 03-gpu/runtimeclass.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: ollama-exporter
  name: ollama-exporter
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ollama-exporter
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ollama-exporter
    spec:
      containers:
      - args:
        - --config
        - /etc/ollama-exporter/ollama-exporter.yml
        # Built locally and pushed to the in-cluster Harbor (registry/ namespace,
        # registry.ash4d.com), so this needs the harbor-pull imagePullSecret below
        # — that Secret is created out-of-band and is NOT in this repo.
        image: registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/ollama-exporter:0.4.0-stream2
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: metrics
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 20
        name: exporter
        ports:
        - containerPort: 9400
          name: metrics
        - containerPort: 9401
          name: proxy
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: metrics
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '1'
            memory: 256Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 64Mi
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /etc/ollama-exporter
          name: config
          readOnly: true
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: harbor-pull
      volumes:
      - configMap:
          name: ollama-exporter-config
        name: config
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: ollama-exporter
  name: ollama-exporter
  namespace: ai
spec:
  # Pinned LB IP — dashboards and out-of-cluster scrapes target it directly.
  loadBalancerIP: 192.168.7.160
  ports:
  - name: metrics
    port: 9400
    targetPort: metrics
  - name: proxy
    port: 9401
    targetPort: proxy
  selector:
    app: ollama-exporter
  type: LoadBalancer
---
# Exporter config. Note ollama_url points at ollama's ClusterIP service, and
# exclude_paths keeps the exporter's own 15s polling out of the proxy metrics.

# docs-rag-mcp — MCP server for semantic search over the Milvus doc corpora
# populated by the 08-indexer CronJobs (k8s_docs, suse_docs, logicpro_docs).
#
# Successor to the old `retrieval-tool` FastAPI service, which no longer exists
# on the cluster: same job, but streamable-HTTP MCP instead of OpenAPI, so mcpo
# can proxy it to Open WebUI AND Claude/Cowork sessions can point at it directly.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: docs-rag-mcp
  name: docs-rag-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: docs-rag-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: docs-rag-mcp
    spec:
      containers:
      - env:
        # PYTHONPATH is vestigial: the v1 pod pip-installed deps into an
        # emptyDir at /deps. The v2 image bakes them in, so nothing mounts
        # there any more — harmless, and left as-is to match the live pod.
        - name: PYTHONPATH
          value: /deps
        - name: PYTHONUNBUFFERED
          value: '1'
        # Query embeddings go through ollama-exporter's pass-through proxy
        # (9401), not ollama directly, so retrieval traffic is counted in the
        # exporter's metrics. See 04-ollama/ollama-exporter/.
        - name: OLLAMA_URL
          value: http://ollama-exporter.ai.svc.cluster.local:9401
        - name: MILVUS_URI
          value: http://milvus.ai.svc.cluster.local:19530
        # Must stay identical to what the indexers embedded with, or the
        # similarity scores are meaningless.
        - name: EMBED_MODEL
          value: nomic-embed-text
        - name: EMBED_DIM
          value: '768'
        - name: PORT
          value: '8080'
        # Built locally and imported into containerd on the node — never pushed
        # to a registry, hence pullPolicy Never. v2 bakes in server.py and its
        # deps; the ConfigMap below is the source of record for that script.
        image: localhost/docs-rag-mcp:v2
        imagePullPolicy: Never
        livenessProbe:
          initialDelaySeconds: 120
          periodSeconds: 30
          tcpSocket:
            port: 8080
        name: server
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
          name: http
        readinessProbe:
          failureThreshold: 12
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
          tcpSocket:
            port: 8080
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '1'
            memory: 1Gi
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 256Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: docs-rag-mcp
  name: docs-rag-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: docs-rag-mcp
  # LoadBalancer (not ClusterIP like the other MCP servers) so Claude/Cowork
  # sessions outside the cluster can reach /mcp without going through mcpo.
  type: LoadBalancer
---
# server.py. NOT mounted by the Deployment above — the v2 image bakes it in —
# but kept applied as the versioned source of record for the next image build.
# Edit here, rebuild, re-import; see README.md.

# docs-rag-mcp — semantic search over the lab's cached doc corpora (MCP)

Streamable-HTTP MCP server over the Milvus collections that the `08-indexer`
CronJobs populate: `k8s_docs` (kubernetes/website), `suse_docs` (12 SUSE /
openSUSE repos), `logicpro_docs`. Two tools — `docs_search` and
`docs_list_sources` — returning markdown with real upstream URLs so results are
citable rather than repo-relative paths.

GPU-light by design: `nomic-embed-text` query embeddings via Ollama, CPU vector
search in Milvus, so the big chat model never runs during retrieval. Query
embeddings must use the same model the indexers embedded with (768-dim) or the
similarity scores are meaningless.

Reached three ways: mcpo proxies it into Open WebUI as OpenAPI tools, the
LoadBalancer service (`192.168.7.159:8080`) serves `/mcp` to Claude/Cowork
sessions outside the cluster, and in-cluster clients use the ClusterIP name.

Supersedes the old `retrieval-tool` FastAPI service (OpenAPI, `/search` +
`/search_all`), which is gone from the cluster.

`server.py` lives in the `docs-rag-mcp-src` ConfigMap in `docs-rag-mcp.yaml`.
The v2 image bakes it in, so the ConfigMap is not mounted — it is the versioned
source of record for the next build:

    kubectl -n ai get cm docs-rag-mcp-src -o jsonpath='{.data.server\.py}' > server.py
    docker build -t localhost/docs-rag-mcp:v2 .
    docker save localhost/docs-rag-mcp:v2 | sudo k3s ctr -n k8s.io images import -
    kubectl -n ai rollout restart deploy/docs-rag-mcp

# Startup hook run by comfyui-nvidia-docker's init on every container start
# (after venv/ComfyUI setup, before the server launches). Keeps pip deps
# self-healing across image upgrades and venv rebuilds.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui
  name: comfyui-user-script
  namespace: ai
data:
  user_script.bash: |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e
    PIP=/comfy/mnt/venv/bin/pip

    # 1. Self-heal: ensure every custom node's python deps are present
    #    (no-op when satisfied; rebuilds them after a fresh venv).
    for req in /basedir/custom_nodes/*/requirements.txt; do
      [ -f "$req" ] && $PIP install --no-cache-dir -r "$req"
    done

    # 2. Version pins LAST so they win over whatever the steps above pulled.
    #    torch 2.6 (cu124) breaks with transformers >= 4.54
    #    (torch.float8_e8m0fnu). Revisit when the image moves to torch >= 2.7.
    $PIP install --no-cache-dir "transformers==4.51.3"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui
  name: comfyui
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: comfyui
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: comfyui
    spec:
      containers:
      # NOTE: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (GPU pin) is deliberately NOT managed
      # here — it is set live on the cluster and switched between GPUs as
      # needed. If a future sync strips it, re-add via kubectl edit/patch.
      - env:
        - name: COMFY_CMDLINE_EXTRA
          value: --listen 0.0.0.0
        - name: WANTED_UID
          value: '1024'
        - name: WANTED_GID
          value: '1024'
        - name: BASE_DIRECTORY

# NOT APPLIED — reference only. Renamed .yaml.txt so Fleet never bundles it,
# same trick as 09-mcp/github-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt.
#
# Added to the repo in 77eed5e ("persist deps across pod upgrades") but never
# applied to the cluster: as of 2026-07-29 there is no comfyui-user-script
# ConfigMap in the ai namespace and the live Deployment mounts no user script.
# It is parked here so wiring Fleet cannot push an untested change into a GPU
# workload — if this is still wanted, apply and verify it by hand first, then
# fold the ConfigMap plus its volume/volumeMount back into comfyui.yaml.
#
# Startup hook run by comfyui-nvidia-docker's init on every container start
# (after venv/ComfyUI setup, before the server launches). Keeps pip deps
# self-healing across image upgrades and venv rebuilds.
#
# Mount it back with:
#   volumes:
#   - name: user-script
#     configMap:
#       defaultMode: 0o755
#       name: comfyui-user-script
#   volumeMounts:
#   - mountPath: /comfy/mnt/user_script.bash
#     name: user-script
#     subPath: user_script.bash
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  labels:
    app: comfyui
  name: comfyui-user-script
  namespace: ai
data:
  user_script.bash: |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e
    PIP=/comfy/mnt/venv/bin/pip

    # 1. Self-heal: ensure every custom node's python deps are present
    #    (no-op when satisfied; rebuilds them after a fresh venv).
    for req in /basedir/custom_nodes/*/requirements.txt; do
      [ -f "$req" ] && $PIP install --no-cache-dir -r "$req"
    done

    # 2. Version pins LAST so they win over whatever the steps above pulled.
    #    torch 2.6 (cu124) breaks with transformers >= 4.54
    #    (torch.float8_e8m0fnu). Revisit when the image moves to torch >= 2.7.
    $PIP install --no-cache-dir "transformers==4.51.3"

  # (see 04-ollama/values.yaml), so the two cannot both be resident. Scale to 1
  # when you want ComfyUI and can afford to evict ollama's model.

    matchLabels:
      app: comfyui

      labels:
        app: comfyui
    spec:
      containers:
      # Env order below matches the live pod spec so a diff against the cluster

        # GPU pin: the Tesla V100 32GB, NOT GPU 0 (a GTX 1070, 8GB). Declared

        - name: USE_UV
          value: 'true'

          value: compute,utility
        - name: WANTED_UID
          value: '1024'
        - name: WANTED_GID

# Two containers in one pod, sharing the hermes-data PVC:
#   hermes-agent — the Nous Research agent + its API server on 8642
#   hermes-webui — a separate community UI on 8787, which reads the agent's
#                  state directly off the shared volume rather than over HTTP.
# They are co-located (not two Deployments) because hermes-webui needs both the
# agent's state dir AND a copy of the agent source tree, so splitting them would
# mean an RWX volume. Recreate strategy — single RWO Longhorn writer.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: hermes-agent
  name: hermes-agent
  namespace: hermes
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: hermes-agent
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: hermes-agent
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - hermes
        - gateway
        - run
        env:
        - name: HERMES_UID
          value: '1000'
        - name: HERMES_GID
          value: '1000'
        - name: API_SERVER_ENABLED
          value: 'true'
        - name: API_SERVER_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        - name: API_SERVER_PORT
          value: '8642'
        - name: API_SERVER_KEY
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: key
              name: hermes-api-key
        - name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
              name: hermes-slack
        - name: SLACK_APP_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: SLACK_APP_TOKEN
              name: hermes-slack
        - name: SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS
              name: hermes-slack
        image: docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: hermes-agent
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8642
          name: api
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '2'
            memory: 2Gi
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 512Mi
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /opt/data
          name: data
      # The UI runs as uid 10000 (hence the fix-perms init container) and wants
      # the agent's source tree on disk to introspect it — supplied by the
      # copy-agent-src init container via the agent-src emptyDir.
      - env:
        - name: WANTED_UID
          value: '10000'
        - name: WANTED_GID
          value: '10000'
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_PORT
          value: '8787'

        # a Secret here because this repo is public and Fleet renders it into a
        # Bundle on the controller. Create the Secret (see
        # hermes-webui.secret.example.yaml.txt) BEFORE enabling this path, or
        # the pod will not start. The value that was in the live spec should be
        # treated as compromised and rotated.
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: password
              name: hermes-webui
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_STATE_DIR
          value: /home/hermeswebui/.hermes/webui
        - name: HERMES_NIX_BUILD
          value: '1'
        image: ghcr.io/nesquena/hermes-webui:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: hermes-webui
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8787
          name: webui
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '1'
            memory: 1Gi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 256Mi
        volumeMounts:
        # Same PVC as the agent, mounted where the UI expects its state.
        - mountPath: /home/hermeswebui/.hermes
          name: data
        - mountPath: /home/hermeswebui/.hermes/hermes-agent
          name: agent-src
      initContainers:
      # The PVC is created root-owned; hermes-webui runs as 10000 and cannot
      # write its state dir without this.
      - command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - chown -R 10000:10000 /opt/data && echo chowned-to-10000
        image: busybox:1.36
        name: fix-perms
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 0
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /opt/data
          name: data
      # Stages the agent source out of the agent image into a shared emptyDir so
      # hermes-webui can read it without the two images being the same.
      - command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - cp -a /opt/hermes/. /agent-src/ && echo agent-source-copied
        image: docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: copy-agent-src
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /agent-src
          name: agent-src
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: hermes-data
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: agent-src

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: hermes-agent
  name: hermes-agent
  namespace: hermes
spec:
  ports:
  - name: api
    port: 8642
    targetPort: 8642
  - name: webui
    port: 8787
    targetPort: 8787

  # is not behind the ingress — only the UI on 8787 is.
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: hermes-agent
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:

        pathType: Prefix
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - hermes.ash4d.com
    secretName: hermes-ash4d-tls

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: hermes-data
  namespace: hermes
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi
  storageClassName: longhorn

+        # hermes-webui.secret.example.yaml.txt) BEFORE enabling this path, or the
+        # pod will not start. The value currently in the live spec has been
+        # sitting in plaintext and should be rotated, not reused.
+        # Same PVC as the agent, mounted where the UI expects its state.
+      # The PVC is created root-owned; hermes-webui runs as 10000 and cannot
+      # write its state dir without this.
+      # Stages the agent source out of the agent image into a shared emptyDir so
+      # hermes-webui can read it without the two images having to be the same.
+  # LoadBalancer (192.168.7.161): the API on 8642 is consumed off-cluster and is
+  # not behind the ingress — only the UI on 8787 is.
+    # cert-manager issues/renews hermes-ash4d-tls via the DNS-01 issuer.
+      # 8787 = the UI. The agent API on 8642 is deliberately not exposed here.

spec:

      - command:
        - gateway
        - run

        - name: HERMES_GID

        - name: API_SERVER_ENABLED

        - name: API_SERVER_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        - name: API_SERVER_PORT
          value: '8642'
        - name: API_SERVER_KEY

        - name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
              name: hermes-slack
        - name: SLACK_APP_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:

              name: hermes-slack
        - name: SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS

# Two containers in one pod, sharing the hermes-data PVC:
#   hermes-agent — the Nous Research agent + its API server on 8642
#   hermes-webui — a separate community UI on 8787, which reads the agent's
#                  state directly off the shared volume rather than over HTTP.
# They are co-located (not two Deployments) because hermes-webui needs both the
# agent's state dir AND a copy of the agent source tree, so splitting them would
# mean an RWX volume. Recreate strategy — single RWO Longhorn writer.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: hermes-agent
  name: hermes-agent
  namespace: hermes
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: hermes-agent
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: hermes-agent
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - hermes
        - gateway
        - run
        env:
        - name: HERMES_UID
          value: '1000'
        - name: HERMES_GID
          value: '1000'
        - name: API_SERVER_ENABLED
          value: 'true'
        - name: API_SERVER_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        - name: API_SERVER_PORT
          value: '8642'
        - name: API_SERVER_KEY
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: key
              name: hermes-api-key
        - name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
              name: hermes-slack
        - name: SLACK_APP_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: SLACK_APP_TOKEN
              name: hermes-slack
        - name: SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS
              name: hermes-slack
        image: docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: hermes-agent
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8642
          name: api
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '2'
            memory: 2Gi
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 512Mi
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /opt/data
          name: data
      # The UI runs as uid 10000 (hence the fix-perms init container) and wants
      # the agent's source tree on disk to introspect it — supplied by the
      # copy-agent-src init container via the agent-src emptyDir.
      - env:
        - name: WANTED_UID
          value: '10000'
        - name: WANTED_GID
          value: '10000'
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_PORT
          value: '8787'
        # NOTE: this is a LITERAL value on the live pod. Externalised to a Secret
        # here because this repo is public and Fleet renders manifests into a
        # Bundle on the controller. Create the Secret (see
        # hermes-webui.secret.example.yaml.txt) BEFORE enabling this path, or the
        # pod will not start. The value currently in the live spec has been
        # sitting in plaintext and should be rotated, not reused.
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: password
              name: hermes-webui
        - name: HERMES_WEBUI_STATE_DIR
          value: /home/hermeswebui/.hermes/webui
        - name: HERMES_NIX_BUILD
          value: '1'
        image: ghcr.io/nesquena/hermes-webui:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: hermes-webui
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8787
          name: webui
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '1'
            memory: 1Gi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 256Mi
        volumeMounts:
        # Same PVC as the agent, mounted where the UI expects its state.
        - mountPath: /home/hermeswebui/.hermes
          name: data
        - mountPath: /home/hermeswebui/.hermes/hermes-agent
          name: agent-src
      initContainers:
      # The PVC is created root-owned; hermes-webui runs as 10000 and cannot
      # write its state dir without this.
      - command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - chown -R 10000:10000 /opt/data && echo chowned-to-10000
        image: busybox:1.36
        name: fix-perms
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 0
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /opt/data
          name: data
      # Stages the agent source out of the agent image into a shared emptyDir so
      # hermes-webui can read it without the two images having to be the same.
      - command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - cp -a /opt/hermes/. /agent-src/ && echo agent-source-copied
        image: docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        name: copy-agent-src
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /agent-src
          name: agent-src
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: hermes-data
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: agent-src
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: hermes-agent
  name: hermes-agent
  namespace: hermes
spec:
  ports:
  - name: api
    port: 8642
    targetPort: 8642
  - name: webui
    port: 8787
    targetPort: 8787
  selector:
    app: hermes-agent
  # LoadBalancer (192.168.7.161): the API on 8642 is consumed off-cluster and is
  # not behind the ingress — only the UI on 8787 is.
  type: LoadBalancer
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    # cert-manager issues/renews hermes-ash4d-tls via the DNS-01 issuer.
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns
  name: hermes-agent
  namespace: hermes
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
  - host: hermes.ash4d.com
    http:
      paths:
      # 8787 = the UI. The agent API on 8642 is deliberately not exposed here.
      - backend:
          service:
            name: hermes-agent
            port:
              number: 8787
        path: /
        pathType: Prefix
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - hermes.ash4d.com
    secretName: hermes-ash4d-tls
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: hermes-data
  namespace: hermes
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi
  storageClassName: longhorn

############ 06-milvus/README.md ############ # 06 — Milvus (standalone) + Attu helm repo add milvus https://zilliztech.github.io/milvus-helm/ helm upgrade --install milvus milvus/milvus -n ai -f values.yaml kubectl apply -f attu/attu.yaml Standalone mode (no Pulsar), single etcd replica, MinIO standalone — sized for a single-node lab. Attu provides the admin UI over the Milvus gRPC port. It lives in `attu/` as its own Fleet bundle, separate from the Milvus Helm release. ############ 07-comfyui/README.md ############ # 07 — ComfyUI + filebrowser kubectl apply -f comfyui.yaml `mmartial/comfyui-nvidia-docker` with a Longhorn-backed basedir; requests one GPU via the device plugin. The filebrowser deployment shares the PVC for model/workflow management. `glm-model-pvc` holds large model files. ############ 08-indexer/README.md ############ # 08 — k8s-docs-indexer (CronJob) Single-file Python service (source recovered from the running image after the original Dockerfile was lost — see Dockerfile header). manifest is a placeholder — rotate it if the service ever leaves the trusted LAN.

`k8s-mcp-server.yaml` ships the ServiceAccount plus a cluster-scoped
ClusterRole/Binding limited to `get`/`list`/`watch`. That RBAC — not the
container's `--read-only` flag — is what actually makes the server read-only, so
keep the verbs as they are.

`docs-rag/` replaces the old `retrieval-tool` FastAPI service, which is gone from
the cluster: same Milvus-backed retrieval, but streamable-HTTP MCP instead of
OpenAPI, so external Claude/Cowork sessions can use it directly as well as
through mcpo."""),

# 04 — Ollama (otwld/ollama-helm)

    helm repo add ollama-helm https://helm.otwld.com/
    helm upgrade --install ollama ollama-helm/ollama --version 1.67.0 -n ai --create-namespace -f values.yaml

Key choices: Tesla V100 (32 GB) pinned by GPU UUID; flash attention + q8_0 KV
cache to fit useful contexts; `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=98304` (96k) with
`OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2`; LoadBalancer at `192.168.7.153:11434` so LAN clients
(Claude Code via ollama-code-mcp, the Xcode instance) reach it directly. 200Gi
Longhorn PV for models.

## Context length

`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` is **per parallel slot**, not a pool divided among them.
Resolved 2026-07-30 against the live pod: 262144 with `NUM_PARALLEL=1` held
~30.4 GiB of the 31.75 GiB card, so two slots at that context would need ~43 GiB.

History:

- 2026-07-18 — set to 65536 because hermes-agent (`10-hermes`) needs at least
  64k. Below that, hermes auto-detected 262144 from model metadata, packed
  prompts to fit, and every response came back `finish_reason='length'`.
- 2026-07-29 — an out-of-band `kubectl edit` raised it to 262144. That pushed
  ~703 MiB of qwen3-coder:30b onto the CPU and prompt processing fell to
  152 tok/s, declining further as context grew.
- 2026-07-30 — settled at 98304 (96k) x 2 slots. Still clears the 64k floor.

## VRAM budget

Primary model is `qwen3-coder:30b` (30.5B MoE, Q4_K_M, 48 layers, 4 KV heads,
head_dim 128 → 49152 KV elements/token).

| Component | Size |
|---|---|
| Card (Tesla V100 32GB) | 31.75 GiB |
| Weights | 17.3 GiB |
| KV cache, q8_0 @ 96k x 2 | 9.56 GiB |
| Compute buffers (estimated) | ~1.0 GiB |
| Headroom | ~3.3 GiB |

q8_0 costs 51 KiB/token, so KV scales as `ctx x slots x 51 KiB`. Alternatives in
the same envelope: 112k x 2 (11.16 GiB), 128k x 2 (12.75 GiB, no headroom),
64k x 3 (9.56 GiB). Dropping KV to f16 doubles every figure above and will not
fit.

After any change to context, parallelism, or KV cache type, confirm the model is
entirely on GPU:

    curl -s http://192.168.7.153:11434/api/ps | jq '.models[] | {size, size_vram, context_length}'

`size_vram` must equal `size`. Any gap is CPU offload — reduce context or slots.

## Upgrade procedure

Scale to zero first. On 2026-07-16 an in-place change wedged the old ollama
process, which ignored SIGTERM and took the V100 off the bus ("GPU is lost",
`nvidia-smi` hung on sdf1). Force-deleting the stuck pod then produced a
~250-pod `UnexpectedAdmissionError` ReplicaSet storm.

    kubectl --context default -n ai scale deploy/ollama --replicas=0
    kubectl --context default -n ai rollout status deploy/ollama --timeout=180s
    helm --kube-context default upgrade --install ollama ollama-helm/ollama \
      --version 1.67.0 -n ai -f values.yaml

`helm list` looks empty for sdf1 releases unless you pass `--kube-context default`
— the Mac defaults to the `rancher` context (khyron).

## Fleet

`fleet.yaml` sets `takeOwnership: true` and Fleet watches this bundle. If Fleet
syncs from git before a manual `helm upgrade`, Fleet applies the change and the
manual command becomes a no-op. Decide which one is driving before running either.

# Fleet Wiring — Handoff / Resume Notes

Turning `lab-fleet` from published reference config into **GitOps that Rancher
Fleet deploys** to this cluster. Full plan (private): Cowork workspace
`_portfolio/ash4d-lab/fleet-wiring-plan.md`. This file is the short resume note
for picking the work back up.

Verified against the live cluster **2026-07-29**.

## Topology

- **Rancher controller** — `v2.14.3` at `https://rancher.ash4d.com`
  (**192.168.7.148**, separate host). GitRepo/Bundle objects live here, and the
  local `kubectl` context named **`rancher`** already has API access to them —
  no Rancher API token needed (see Phase 0).
- **This cluster** — `sdf1`, downstream `c-nnzn9` at **192.168.7.149**.
  `fleet-agent v0.15.4` is Ready but idle — its only bundle is its own
  `fleet-agent-c-nnzn9`, so no GitRepo targets it yet.
- Deploy source is **`lab-fleet` directly**, not `ash4d.com/lab` (Fleet doesn't
  init git submodules, so a GitRepo on `ash4d.com` would clone an empty gitlink).
  Public repo → no clone secret needed.
- Note the downstream cluster has **no Fleet CRDs** — that is normal for this
  Fleet version (`EXPERIMENTAL_COPY_RESOURCES_DOWNSTREAM=false`). Bundle state is
  read on the controller, not here. See Verify below.

## ✅ Phase 1 — DONE (committed AND pushed to `main`)

Every deployable numbered dir has a `fleet.yaml`:

- **Helm bundles** (`takeOwnership: true`, versions pinned to the running
  releases so Fleet adopts instead of upgrading):
  metallb `0.16.1`, longhorn `1.12.0`, nvdp `0.19.2`, dcgm-exporter `4.8.2`,
  ollama `1.67.0`, open-webui `14.8.0`, milvus `5.0.22`. **All seven were
  re-verified against `helm get values` on 2026-07-29 — chart versions and
  user-supplied values match the repo exactly.**
- **Raw-manifest bundles:** comfyui, the three doc indexers, mcp, hermes, emby,
  node-red, resilio, plus metallb pools, the nvidia RuntimeClass, attu,
  ollama-exporter, and docs-rag.
- Where a dir had a chart **and** raw manifests, the raw manifests were moved
  into a sibling subdir so each chart owns its own bundle path (Fleet = one
  chart per path): `01-networking/pools/`, `03-gpu/{dcgm-exporter,runtimeclass}/`,
  `06-milvus/attu/`, `04-ollama/ollama-exporter/`.
- Placeholder/unapplied manifests are renamed `.yaml.txt` so Fleet never applies
  them: `09-mcp/github-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt`,
  `10-hermes/hermes-webui.secret.example.yaml.txt`,
  `07-comfyui/comfyui-user-script.yaml.txt`.
- `00-host` and `14-cluster-mgmt` stay docs-only (no `fleet.yaml`). Traefik is
  k3s-bundled and not Fleet-managed (`traefik-values.yaml` is reference only).

## ✅ Phase 0 — Enable CD on the controller: ALREADY DONE

The earlier note here assumed the `fleet` feature was off and that a Rancher API
token was needed. Both were wrong as of 2026-07-29:

- The `fleet` feature is **enabled** (`features.management.cattle.io/fleet`:
  `spec.value` unset, `status.default: true`). Nothing to PUT.
- `kubectl --context rancher` reaches the GitRepo/Bundle/BundleDeployment CRDs
  directly, so the whole flow can be driven with `kubectl` — no `RTOKEN`, no
  `/v3/features` call.
- `c-nnzn9` is registered in workspace **`fleet-default`**.
- **Working precedent already on the controller:** GitRepo
  `fleet-default/ash4d-site` → `https://github.com/darthzen/ash4d.com`, branch
  `main`, `paths: ["deploy"]`, target `clusterSelector.matchLabels.site=ash4d`.
  It is Ready 1/1 — but it targets `cluster-ee8f7993b3a6` (a *different*
  downstream, last seen 2026-07-17), **not** `c-nnzn9`. Copy its shape, don't
  reuse its selector.

**Target label for this cluster:** `c-nnzn9` already carries a bespoke
`ash4d-lab: ""` label — use that rather than
`management.cattle.io/cluster-name`, which is Rancher-managed.

```yaml
targets:
  - clusterSelector:
      matchLabels:
        ash4d-lab: ""
```

## ⏭ Phase 2/3 — GitRepo + staged rollout (approve each widen)

Create a GitRepo in `fleet-default` pointing at
`https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet`, branch `main`. **Start narrow** with a
single low-risk `paths:` entry, then widen one component at a time, riskiest
last:

| Order | Component(s) | Risk | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `12-node-red`, `13-resilio`, `11-emby` | low | app layer, easy rollback |
| 2 | `07-comfyui`, `09-mcp`, `10-hermes` | low–med | Secrets must pre-exist |
| 3 | `08-indexer`, `04-ollama/ollama-exporter` | low–med | CronJobs + Harbor pull secret |
| 4 | `05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`, `04-ollama` | med | helm adopt; watch pod churn |
| 5 | `01-networking`, `03-gpu` | med–high | MetalLB/Traefik + GPU; net blips |
| 6 | `02-longhorn` | **high** | storage — adopt last, or monitor-only |

At each step: add the path, let Fleet render, confirm the BundleDeployment goes
Ready, spot-check the workload, proceed. Roll back by removing the path.

Leave `correctDrift` unset at first. Turning it on makes Fleet revert
out-of-band `kubectl edit`s — desirable eventually, but it will fight the
hand-tuning habits this cluster has (see the ComfyUI and Ollama notes below).

## Watch-outs

- **Helm adoption is the real hazard.** `helm get manifest` vs `helm template`
  should match before enabling a helm path; adopt one release at a time.
- **Missing Secrets = stuck bundles.** Create these before enabling the
  corresponding path:
  | Secret | Namespace | Needed by | Exists? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `github-mcp-token` | `ai` | github-mcp-server | ✅ |
  | `harbor-pull` | `ai` | ollama-exporter (Harbor image) | ✅ |
  | `hermes-api-key`, `hermes-slack` | `hermes` | hermes-agent | ✅ |
  | `hermes-webui` | `hermes` | hermes-webui container | ❌ **create first** |
  | `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY` | `ai` | open-webui | check before Phase 4 |
- **`hermes-webui` password.** The live Deployment carries
  `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` as a plaintext env value. `10-hermes/hermes.yaml`
  reads it from a Secret instead — this repo is public and Fleet renders
  manifests into a Bundle on the controller. Create the Secret with a **new**
  password; treat the live one as compromised. This is the **only** intentional
  divergence between the repo and live state.
- **ComfyUI is declared at `replicas: 0`,** matching the cluster — it pins the
  same V100 that Ollama holds. Scale it by editing the manifest, not
  `kubectl scale`, or Fleet reconciles it back.
- **Locally-built images** (`localhost/k8s-docs-indexer:v2`,
  `localhost/docs-rag-mcp:v2`) use `imagePullPolicy: Never` and exist only in
  the node's containerd. Fleet deploys the manifests; it does not build or
  distribute these images.

## Verify

Controller (this is where bundle state actually lives):

```bash
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-fleet \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.summary}'
kubectl --context rancher get bundles -A
kubectl --context rancher -n cluster-fleet-default-c-nnzn9-eaf6ebdbb298 \
  get bundledeployments
```

The old note said to run `kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system get bundledeployments`
**downstream** — that fails here (`the server doesn't have a resource type
"bundledeployments"`), because this Fleet version keeps BundleDeployments on the
controller in the per-cluster namespace shown above.

## Drift reconciliation log

`2026-07-29` — full live-vs-repo audit before wiring anything. All seven Helm
releases were already exact. Raw manifests had drifted, and the repo has been
corrected to match live:

- **New to the repo:** `suse-docs-indexer` + `logicpro-docs-indexer` (CronJobs,
  ConfigMap-mounted scripts, state PVCs); `ollama-exporter` (metrics on 9400 +
  Ollama pass-through proxy on 9401); `k8s-mcp-server` ServiceAccount and
  cluster-scoped read-only RBAC; the `attu` and `hermes-agent` Ingresses;
  `comfyui-filebrowser-config` PVC.
- **`retrieval-tool` → `docs-rag`:** the FastAPI service is gone from the
  cluster, replaced by the `docs-rag-mcp` MCP server. Old dir and build inputs
  removed.
- **Corrected to match live:** ComfyUI `replicas: 1` → `0` and its V100 UUID pin
  now declared; filebrowser config emptyDir → PVC and its service port
  `8080` → `80`; `glm-model-pvc` missing `storageClassName: longhorn`; attu
  service `LoadBalancer` → `ClusterIP`; hermes gained its `hermes-webui`
  container, two init containers, `LoadBalancer` service and 8787 port;
  `k8s-docs-indexer` image/pull policy; all indexers and docs-rag now embed via
  the exporter proxy on 9401; `mcpo` config gained its `docs` entry; MetalLB
  service annotations; Emby's bogus `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` limit removed (it pins
  by UUID, and the live pod has no such request).
- **Parked, not applied:** `07-comfyui/comfyui-user-script.yaml.txt`. Added to
  the repo in `77eed5e` but never applied — there is no `comfyui-user-script`
  ConfigMap on the cluster and the live pod mounts no user script. Kept as
  reference so wiring Fleet cannot push an untested change into a GPU workload.

Every manifest was confirmed with `kubectl diff` after editing: clean except the
deliberate `hermes-webui` Secret substitution.

## Out of scope (not in this repo, running on the cluster)

These namespaces have live workloads with no `lab-fleet` bundle. They are
deliberately untracked here, not oversights — decide separately whether any
should be adopted: `lab-memory` (karakeep + MCP servers), `registry` (Harbor),
`buzz`, `trading-agent`, `nemoclaw` + `nemoclaw-sandboxes`, `openshell`,
`ollama-code`, `ash4d-origin`, `agent-sandbox-system`, `managed-agent`, and the
Rancher-managed `cattle-*` / `cert-manager` stacks.

# Fleet Wiring — Handoff / Resume Notes

Turning `lab-fleet` from published reference config into **GitOps that Rancher
Fleet deploys** to this cluster. Full plan (private): Cowork workspace
`_portfolio/ash4d-lab/fleet-wiring-plan.md`. This file is the short resume note
for picking the work back up.

## Topology

- **Rancher controller** — `v2.14.2` at `https://rancher.ash4d.com`
  (**192.168.7.148**, separate host). GitRepo/Bundle objects live here.
- **This cluster** — `sdf1`, downstream `c-nnzn9` at **192.168.7.149**.
  `fleet-agent v0.15.2` is Ready but idle — no GitRepo targets it yet.
- Deploy source is **`lab-fleet` directly**, not `ash4d.com/lab` (Fleet doesn't
  init git submodules, so a GitRepo on `ash4d.com` would clone an empty gitlink).
  Public repo → no clone secret needed.

## ✅ Phase 1 — DONE (committed to `main`, not yet pushed)

Every deployable numbered dir has a `fleet.yaml`:

- **Helm bundles** (`takeOwnership: true`, versions pinned to the running
  releases so Fleet adopts instead of upgrading):
  metallb `0.16.1`, longhorn `1.12.0`, nvdp `0.19.2`, dcgm-exporter `4.8.2`,
  ollama `1.67.0` (confirmed live), open-webui `14.8.0`, milvus `5.0.22`.
- **Raw-manifest bundles:** comfyui, indexer, mcp, hermes, emby, node-red,
  resilio, plus metallb pools, the nvidia RuntimeClass, and attu.
- Where a dir had a chart **and** raw manifests, the raw manifests were moved
  into a sibling subdir so each chart owns its own bundle path (Fleet = one
  chart per path): `01-networking/pools/`, `03-gpu/{dcgm-exporter,runtimeclass}/`,
  `06-milvus/attu/`.
- `09-mcp/github-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml` → `.yaml.txt` so Fleet never
  applies the placeholder Secret.
- `00-host` and `14-cluster-mgmt` stay docs-only (no `fleet.yaml`). Traefik is
  k3s-bundled and not Fleet-managed (`traefik-values.yaml` is reference only).

**Not yet pushed** — push `lab-fleet` `main` to the remote before Fleet can
clone it.

## ⏭ Phase 0 — Enable CD on the controller (needs Rancher API token for .148)

1. Mint a Rancher API token (UI: avatar → Account & API Keys → Create API Key,
   no scope), export as `RTOKEN`.
2. Check the `fleet` feature (agent env hinted `fleet=false`); enable if off:
   `PUT https://rancher.ash4d.com/v3/features/fleet -d '{"value":true}'`.
3. Confirm the cluster's Fleet workspace (likely `fleet-default`) and a stable
   target label (e.g. `management.cattle.io/cluster-name: c-nnzn9`).
- **Acceptance:** `GET /v1/fleet.cattle.io.gitrepos` returns 200 and the cluster
  is listed under a Fleet workspace with a targetable label.

## ⏭ Phase 2/3 — GitRepo + staged rollout (needs token; approve each widen)

Create a GitRepo in the Fleet workspace pointing at
`https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet`, branch `main`. **Start narrow** with a
single low-risk `paths:` entry, then widen one component at a time, riskiest
last:

| Order | Component(s) | Risk | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `12-node-red`, `13-resilio`, `11-emby` | low | app layer, easy rollback |
| 2 | `07-comfyui`, `09-mcp`, `10-hermes` | low–med | Secrets must pre-exist |
| 3 | `05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`, `04-ollama` | med | helm adopt; watch pod churn |
| 4 | `01-networking`, `03-gpu` | med–high | MetalLB/Traefik + GPU; net blips |
| 5 | `02-longhorn` | **high** | storage — adopt last, or monitor-only |

At each step: add the path, let Fleet render, confirm the BundleDeployment goes
Ready, spot-check the workload, proceed. Roll back by removing the path.

## Watch-outs

- **Helm adoption is the real hazard.** `helm get manifest` vs `helm template`
  should match before enabling a helm path; adopt one release at a time.
- **Missing Secrets = stuck bundles.** Raw manifests use `secretKeyRef`
  (github-mcp token, open-webui `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY`, hermes Slack/API). Create
  them out-of-band before adding those paths.
- Verify: controller `…/gitrepos/fleet-default/lab-fleet | jq .status.summary`;
  downstream `kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system get bundledeployments -A`.

# Installed from chart defaults originally, so `helm get values` is still empty —
# but the running cluster does NOT match chart defaults. Both settings below were
# changed out-of-band (Longhorn UI / CLI), and are declared here so Fleet adopts
# the release instead of reverting them.

# longhorn-storageclass ConfigMap and the default-replica-count setting exactly
# as they exist on the cluster.

# This is a single-node cluster. The chart default of 3 replicas cannot be
# satisfied by one node, so every new volume would sit permanently Degraded and
# scheduling would fail once the replica scheduler ran out of distinct nodes.
# Do not raise these without adding nodes.
persistence:
  # numberOfReplicas in the default `longhorn` StorageClass (chart default: 3).
  defaultClassReplicaCount: 1
defaultSettings:
  # Longhorn's global default-replica-count setting (chart default: unset -> 3).

  defaultReplicaCount: 1

4	Fleet deploys** to this cluster. Full plan (private): Cowork workspace

6	for picking the work back up.

8	Verified against the live cluster **2026-07-29**.
9	
10	## Topology
11	
12	- **Rancher controller** — `v2.14.3` at `https://rancher.ash4d.com`
13	  (**192.168.7.148**, separate host). GitRepo/Bundle objects live here, and the
14	  local `kubectl` context named **`rancher`** already has API access to them —
15	  no Rancher API token needed (see Phase 0).
16	- **This cluster** — `sdf1`, downstream `c-nnzn9` at **192.168.7.149**.
17	  `fleet-agent v0.15.4` is Ready but idle — its only bundle is its own
18	  `fleet-agent-c-nnzn9`, so no GitRepo targets it yet.
19	- Deploy source is **`lab-fleet` directly**, not `ash4d.com/lab` (Fleet doesn't
20	  init git submodules, so a GitRepo on `ash4d.com` would clone an empty gitlink).

content.text:
The repo now mirrors the live cluster. I have **not** committed or created the GitRepo — both are your call.

## What I verified

Every workload in the eight repo-owned namespaces, enumerated exhaustively (nothing unaccounted for), then diffed each manifest against live with `kubectl diff` and each Helm release with `helm get manifest`.

**Clean already:** all 7 Helm chart versions, ollama/milvus/metallb/nvdp/dcgm values, emby, node-red, resilio, mcpo/k8s-mcp/github-mcp deployments, MetalLB pools, RuntimeClass.

## Drift found and reconciled

**Missing from the repo entirely** — `ollama-exporter` (metrics 9400 + Ollama proxy 9401, now `04-ollama/ollama-exporter/`); `suse-docs-indexer` and `logicpro-docs-indexer`; `k8s-mcp-server`'s ServiceAccount + read-only ClusterRole; the `attu` and `hermes-agent` Ingresses; `comfyui-filebrowser-config` PVC.

**`retrieval-tool` → `docs-rag`** — the FastAPI service is gone from the cluster, replaced by the `docs-rag-mcp` MCP server. Renamed the dir, dropped the dead build inputs.

**Hermes** was the largest gap: live has a whole second container (`hermes-webui`, port 8787), two init containers, a LoadBalancer service, and an ingress — none of it in the repo.

**Two Helm drifts `helm get values` could not show**, because the live objects were hand-edited while the release still declared the old values:
- open-webui's Ollama URLs pointed at `ollama:11434`; live routes through the exporter proxy on `9401`.
- Longhorn's values said "chart defaults", but the cluster runs **1** volume replica against a chart default of **3**. Adopting that as-written would have left every new volume permanently Degraded on this single-node box.

I've added the `helm get manifest | kubectl diff` check to the wiring doc — comparing values alone misses this class of drift.

Also: ComfyUI `replicas: 1`→`0` (it pins the same V100 Ollama holds), filebrowser emptyDir→PVC and port `8080`→`80`, `glm-model-pvc` missing its storageClass, attu LoadBalancer→ClusterIP, mcpo's missing `docs` entry, MetalLB service annotations, and Emby's phantom `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` limit (the live pod has no GPU request — it pins by UUID).

## Three things needing your decision

1. **`14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md` was materially wrong about the controller.** Phase 0 is already done: the `fleet` feature is enabled, `kubectl --context rancher` reaches the Fleet CRDs directly so **no Rancher API token is needed**, and there's a working GitRepo precedent (`ash4d-site`) — though it targets a *different* downstream. `c-nnzn9` already carries an `ash4d-lab: ""` label, ideal as the target selector. The doc's verify command was also wrong (BundleDeployments live on the controller here, not downstream). All corrected.

2. **Hermes has a plaintext password in its live pod spec.** This is the one intentional repo/live divergence: `hermes.yaml` reads `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` from a `hermes-webui` Secret that **doesn't exist yet**. Create it (with a *new* value — the current one is exposed to anyone with get-deployment rights) before enabling the hermes path.

3. **The ComfyUI user-script from commit `77eed5e` was never applied.** No such ConfigMap exists on the cluster. Rather than delete the work, I parked it as `comfyui-user-script.yaml.txt` (the repo's existing non-applied convention) so wiring Fleet can't push an untested change into a GPU workload. Apply and verify it by hand if you still want it.

Want me to commit this, and then draft the narrow first GitRepo (node-red only) for your review?


One caveat: hermes will restart **once** when adopted, because the pod template changes from an inline `value:` to a `valueFrom:` — the password itself stays identical. Node-red has no such change.

# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), NOT on sdf1 — and is therefore not
