#
# Widen `paths` ONE entry at a time, riskiest last — see FLEET-WIRING.md for the
# order and the per-path prerequisites. Roll back by removing a path.
#
# Bundles are namespace-scoped by design: each path owns the objects in one
# namespace, so a path can be added or removed without touching anything else.
apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: lab-fleet
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main

  # START NARROW. node-red is the whole first step: it is alone in its namespace,
  # has no Secret or CRD prerequisites, and its manifest is byte-identical to the
  # live objects, so adoption should be metadata-only.
  paths:
    - 12-node-red

  # `ash4d-lab` is a bespoke label already on the sdf1 cluster (c-nnzn9). Chosen
  # over management.cattle.io/cluster-name, which Rancher owns and may rewrite.
  # Do NOT reuse site=ash4d — that selector belongs to the ash4d-site GitRepo and
  # resolves to a different downstream cluster.
  targets:
    - clusterSelector:
        matchLabels:
          ash4d-lab: ""

  # correctDrift deliberately OFF for now. Turning it on makes Fleet revert
  # out-of-band `kubectl edit`s, which is the eventual goal but will fight the
  # hand-tuning this cluster is used to (GPU pins, context sizes, replica counts).
  # Enable it only once every path is adopted and verified.
  correctDrift:
    enabled: false

I've stopped short of creating the Fleet object, because it tracks `branch: main` and `main` doesn't have the commit yet.

| Step | State |

Direct-to-`main` push was rejected by the `entire://` proxy, not GitHub — GitHub reports `main` unprotected with no rulesets. Branch pushes go through fine, hence the PR.

## The secret command

```bash
kubectl -n hermes create secret generic hermes-webui \
  --from-literal=password='REDACTED'
```

That's the value already in the live pod, so adoption won't change the credential. No rush — it's only needed before you add the `10-hermes` path, not for node-red.

## Your call on the next step

Once you merge PR #2, I apply one object to the controller and node-red is adopted:

```yaml
paths: [12-node-red]        # nothing else deploys
correctDrift: {enabled: false}
```

Two ways to sequence it:

1. **Merge, then adopt** — the clean path. I apply the Fleet object against `main`.
2. **Test from the branch first** — I point the Fleet object at `fleet-reconcile-live`, confirm node-red adopts with no restart, then you merge and I flip it to `main`. Costs one extra step but proves adoption before anything touches `main`.

I'd suggest (2) if you want to see the "nothing changes" claim demonstrated before committing to it. Either way, node-red's expected outcome is identical: Helm ownership labels appear on the Deployment/Service/PVC, pod UID unchanged, no restart — and I'll verify exactly that.

One housekeeping note: your local `main` is one commit ahead of `origin/main` right now. If you squash-merge the PR, run `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/main` afterward so local main tracks the merged SHA rather than my original commit.

# Fleet GitRepos — one per namespace

These are Fleet **`GitRepo` custom resources** (`gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io`), not
git repositories. Each one points Fleet at the existing `lab-fleet` repo and
lists which paths to render. They live on the **Rancher controller**
(192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`) — not on sdf1 — so they are not part
of any bundle in this repo. Kept here as the versioned source of record.

    kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-node-red.yaml

## Convention: `lab-<namespace>`

One GitRepo per Kubernetes namespace, so each namespace's workloads can be
adopted, rolled back, or paused independently of every other.

| GitRepo | Namespace | Paths | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lab-node-red` | `node-red` | `12-node-red` | low — **start here** |
| `lab-emby` | `emby` | `11-emby` | low |
| `lab-resilio` | `resilio` | `13-resilio` | low |
| `lab-hermes` | `hermes` | `10-hermes` | low–med — needs `hermes-webui` Secret |
| `lab-ai` | `ai` | 8 paths (04→09) | med — add one at a time |
| `lab-metallb-system` | `metallb-system` | `01-networking`, `01-networking/pools` | med–high |
| `lab-nvidia-device-plugin` | `nvidia-device-plugin` | `03-gpu`, `03-gpu/runtimeclass` | med–high |
| `lab-cattle-monitoring-system` | `cattle-monitoring-system` | `03-gpu/dcgm-exporter` | med |
| `lab-longhorn-system` | `longhorn-system` | `02-longhorn` | **highest — adopt last** |

Adopt in that order. Within `lab-ai`, add paths one at a time — raw manifests
(`08-indexer`, `09-mcp`, `07-comfyui`, `06-milvus/attu`,
`04-ollama/ollama-exporter`) before the Helm charts (`04-ollama`,
`05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`).

## Where the convention doesn't map cleanly

`03-gpu` splits across two GitRepos: the device plugin lands in
`nvidia-device-plugin`, but `03-gpu/dcgm-exporter` deploys into
`cattle-monitoring-system` alongside rancher-monitoring. The cluster-scoped
`03-gpu/runtimeclass` has no namespace of its own, so it rides with
`lab-nvidia-device-plugin` — it must land before any GPU pod schedules.

## Why adoption should be a no-op

Every raw-manifest `fleet.yaml` sets `helm.takeOwnership: true`, and every Helm
`fleet.yaml` pins the chart version to the running release. The manifests were
reconciled against live state, so a first sync should only add Helm ownership
labels to the top-level objects — no pod template changes, no restarts.

The one exception is `lab-hermes`: `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` moves from an inline
value to a `secretKeyRef`, which *is* a pod template change, so that pod restarts
once. Seed the Secret with the value already in the live spec and the credential
itself does not change.

`correctDrift` is off in every file. Turn it on only after everything is adopted
and verified — it makes Fleet revert out-of-band `kubectl edit`s, which is the
goal eventually but will fight this cluster's hand-tuning habits.

## Prerequisite: the fleet-agent must be able to register

As of 2026-07-29 it cannot, so **no GitRepo can deploy anything yet**. See the
"fleet-agent registration is broken" section in `../FLEET-WIRING.md`. Verify
first:

    kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get cluster c-nnzn9 \
      -o jsonpath='{.status.agent.lastSeen}'

An empty result means the agent has never checked in and bundles will sit in
`WaitApplied` forever.

Nine GitRepo objects, one per namespace, all validated against the controller:

|---|---|---|
| `lab-node-red` | `node-red` | `12-node-red` |
| `lab-emby` / `lab-resilio` / `lab-hermes` | ditto | one each |
| `lab-ai` | `ai` | 8 paths (04→09) |

| `lab-cattle-monitoring-system` | `cattle-monitoring-system` | 1 |
| `lab-longhorn-system` | `longhorn-system` | 1 |

One wrinkle worth knowing: **`03-gpu` doesn't fit the convention.** Its three pieces land in three different places — device plugin in `nvidia-device-plugin`, dcgm-exporter in `cattle-monitoring-system`, and the RuntimeClass is cluster-scoped with no namespace at all. ## Fleet can't deploy anything yet

I applied `lab-node-red` and it stalled in `WaitApplied` with **no** BundleDeployment status. The agent has never registered:

```
x509: failed to load system roots and no roots provided
```

It's a policy mismatch, not plumbing:

- Network to Rancher: fine (`/ping` → `pong`)
- CA certs in the agent image: present (435 of them)
- Rancher's cert: valid, public Let's Encrypt
- **`agent-tls-mode: strict`** — refuses system roots, demands an explicit CA
- **`apiServerCA` in the bootstrap secret: empty, 0 bytes**

So strict mode is waiting for a CA that was never supplied, even though the cert needs no custom CA at all. This predates our work — it's why the agent was described as "idle" and why `LAST-SEEN` was blank all along.

I deleted the stalled GitRepo. **node-red is provably untouched:** same pod UID `42e62d04`, 0 restarts, generation still 2, no Helm labels.

I did **not** apply either fix, because `agent-tls-mode` is a controller-wide setting on a different host and would affect every downstream agent:

kubectl --context rancher patch settings.management.cattle.io agent-tls-mode \
  --type=merge -p '{"value":"system-store"}'
```

Option B is populating `apiServerCA` with the Let's Encrypt chain and keeping `strict` — scoped to this cluster, but needs redoing on CA rotation.

A is my recommendation. One extra data point: the other downstream cluster last checked in **the same day the Rancher cert was renewed** (Jul 17), so it's likely broken identically — meaning A probably repairs both.

content.text:
**node-red is live on Fleet, and adoption changed nothing.** Pushed to PR #3.

## The fix worked

`agent-tls-mode` → `system-store`. Rancher recreated the agent Deployment, the new pod waited out the old leader lease (~30s), then registered — `fleet-agent` Secret created, `lastSeen` populating, `c-nnzn9` at 2/2 bundles. About two minutes end to end, no workload touched.

Rollback note: the original value was `""` (inheriting `default: strict`), so restoring means `value: ""`, **not** `"strict"`.

## node-red adoption — measured against a pre-captured baseline

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Pod name / UID | `node-red-fbdd4f8fd-q2jbt` / `42e62d04…` | **identical** |
| Pod startTime | 2026-07-20T18:49:13Z | **identical** — never restarted |
| Restarts | 0 | **0** |
| ReplicaSets | one | **same one** |
| Rollout revision | 1 | **1** |
| `kubectl diff` vs repo | clean | **clean** |
| Helm ownership | none | `lab-node-red-12-node-red` |
| Fleet's own verdict | — | `nonModified=true` |

One thing to expect on every remaining namespace: **`metadata.generation` bumps** (2→3 here), which normally signals a spec write. It's Helm rewriting the spec to identical values — the pod-template hash didn't change, no second ReplicaSet appeared, rollout stayed at revision 1, and the ten-day-old pod is still running. Inert, but don't misread it as a restart. I've documented that so it doesn't cause a false alarm later.

## Two corrections to things I said earlier

- I predicted the TLS fix would also repair `cluster-ee8f7993b3a6`. **It didn't** — still stuck at Jul 17 after the patch, so that host is likely just offline. Separate issue, unrelated to sdf1.
- My first registration poll reported "AGENT REGISTERED" prematurely: `get cluster` resolved to `clusters.cluster.x-k8s.io`, and the error text made my emptiness check pass. Use `clusters.fleet.cattle.io` explicitly — noted in the README since it's an easy trap.

## Remaining, in order

`lab-emby` → `lab-resilio` → `lab-hermes` → `lab-ai` (8 paths, one at a time) → `lab-metallb-system` / `lab-nvidia-device-plugin` / `lab-cattle-monitoring-system` → `lab-longhorn-system` last. All nine manifests exist and pass server-side validation.

`lab-emby` and `lab-resilio` are the natural next pair — no prerequisites, and both verified byte-identical to live. `lab-hermes` needs that secret command first, and it's the one path whose pod will genuinely restart.

Once you merge PR #3 — this session is fairly long now, and the remaining namespaces are mechanical repeats of a proven pattern. Worth running `/handoff` and picking up `lab-emby` in a fresh session; the adoption log in `FLEET-WIRING.md` has everything needed to continue.

content.text:
Deleted and cleaned up. Pushed to PR #3.

## What went

`cluster-ee8f7993b3a6` was a **self-registered** Fleet cluster — Rancher never managed it (`clusters.management.cattle.io` only ever listed `sdf1` and `local`). Its namespace held nothing but its own agent BundleDeployment and a registration token, so deleting the Cluster cascaded both away and the namespace terminated cleanly. No orphaned clusterregistrations remain.

Fleet is now down to what you'd expect:

```
fleet-default/c-nnzn9   2 bundles ready   lastSeen 03:12:08
fleet-local/local       1 bundle ready
```

sdf1 unaffected — node-red still the same pod UID `42e62d04`, 0 restarts, bundle 1/1.

## Two things worth flagging

**`ash4d-site` is gone too.** Its GitRepo *and* its bundle were both present in my opening survey and both absent later in the session. My only deletion before this was `lab-fleet`, which wouldn't touch it — so it went by some other route. It was deploying `paths: ["deploy"]` from `github.com/darthzen/ash4d.com`, targeted at the junk cluster via `site=ash4d`. Given the target was junk, it wasn't doing anything useful, but if you expected ash4d.com to be Fleet-managed, it currently isn't.

**Deleting the Cluster object doesn't uninstall the agent** from that host. If it ever comes back online, its fleet-agent will re-register and a new self-registered cluster will appear. If the host still exists somewhere, uninstall fleet-agent there to make this permanent.

Side benefit: `ash4d-lab: ""` now resolves to exactly one cluster, so every remaining GitRepo has an unambiguous target.

## Where you are

- ✅ Repo mirrors live cluster (verified per-manifest and per-Helm-release)
- ✅ fleet-agent registering
- ✅ `lab-node-red` adopted, no-op proven
- ✅ Controller cleaned to one real downstream
- ⏸ 8 GitRepos ready to apply, all server-side validated

Next is `lab-emby` then `lab-resilio` — no prerequisites, both byte-identical to live, same pattern you just watched work.

Two open items carried in the docs: the `hermes-webui` secret before `lab-hermes`, and `agent-tls-mode` now sitting at `system-store` (rollback is `value: ""`, not `"strict"`).

This session is long and the remaining namespaces are mechanical repeats of a now-proven pattern. Once PR #3 is merged, I'd suggest `/handoff` and picking up `lab-emby` fresh — the adoption log in `FLEET-WIRING.md` has the baseline-capture and verification steps written out, so a new session can continue without re-deriving any of it.

 """## Adoption log

`2026-07-29` — **`lab-emby`, `lab-resilio`, `lab-hermes` adopted.** All four
namespaces now Fleet-managed; every BundleDeployment reports
`ready=true, nonModified=true`.

`lab-emby` and `lab-resilio` were clean no-ops on the same evidence as node-red
below: identical pod UIDs and startTimes, restart counts unchanged (emby 2,
resilio 13), rollout revisions unchanged, no new ReplicaSets, `kubectl diff`
clean. Only `metadata.generation` moved (4→5 and 2→3).

### `lab-hermes` needed a manual step first — read this before adopting anything else

Adoption failed outright at first, with Fleet stuck in `ErrApplied`:

```
cannot patch "hermes-agent" with kind Deployment: Deployment.apps "hermes-agent"
is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers[1].env[4].valueFrom: Invalid value: "":
may not be specified when `value` is not empty
```

**Cause.** The repo converts `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` from an inline `value:` to a
`secretKeyRef`. Kubernetes merges `env` lists **by `name`**, so Helm's
strategic-merge patch laid `valueFrom` *on top of* the live `value` instead of
replacing it, and the API server rejects an env var carrying both. Helm could not
emit a directive to delete the live `value`, because the object was not yet
Helm-owned — there was no prior release manifest to diff against. It retried
~16 times, burning Helm revisions, and never touched the Deployment.

**Fix.** Make live match the repo *before* letting Fleet adopt it. A client-side
`kubectl apply` can do what Helm could not, because the live object carried
`kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` containing the inline value,
which gives `apply` the third input it needs for a proper 3-way merge:

```bash
kubectl apply -f 10-hermes/hermes.yaml     # removes value:, adds valueFrom:
kubectl -n hermes rollout status deploy/hermes-agent --timeout=300s
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-hermes \\
  --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"forceSyncGeneration":1}}'
```

Fleet then adopted it immediately. The pod restarted once — expected, since this
*is* a pod template change — and came back with both containers ready, the
credential unchanged (the Secret was seeded from the live value), Deployment at
revision 13, and `kubectl diff` finally clean: the repo's one intentional
divergence is now resolved on the cluster too.

**Generalisation.** Fleet/Helm adoption cannot remove a field that exists on a
live object but not in the repo, when the field is inside a list merged by key and
the object is not yet Helm-owned. Any such divergence must be pre-applied by hand.
Checked the remaining namespaces for the same pattern: **none of them have it**,
because every other manifest was reconciled to match live exactly. hermes was the
only intentional divergence in the repo, and it is now closed.

`2026-07-29` — **`lab-node-red` adopted. Verified no-op.** First namespace on
Fleet. Evidence, before vs after:"""),
